items.title: I reviewed the Apple HomeView, ask me anything
items.summary: The Verge reviews Apple HomeView, testing its tabletop and wall‑mounted versions in various home settings.

items.title: The pricey new Apple TV 4K is still the best streamer around
items.summary: Apple’s new Apple TV 4K delivers the best streaming experience with integrated HomePod surround sound and 4K HDR support.
items.excerpt: I'm sitting in front of my TV, puppy nuzzled up next to me, with four HomePods spread around my living room - two flanking my TV and one at either end of my couch - connected to the brand new Apple TV 4K. Young Anakin Skywalker hits the throttle and flies through the room. There hasn't been an Apple surround sound system until now, and since it was announced, I was excited to try it out. And let me tell you…
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy users value high-quality audio/visual performance and seamless ecosystem integration for premium home entertainment.

items.title: I tried Google’s AI glasses and Meta’s finally got real competition
items.summary: The article reviews Google’s new AI glasses and Meta’s emerging competitors, noting the current skepticism surrounding smart glasses.
items.excerpt: It's a weird time to launch a new pair of smart glasses. These last few years, Meta has been the dominant player in pushing a fragile smart glasses resurgence. Unfortunately, its privacy reputation led to the "pervert glasses" moniker. Smart glasses have never been more unpopular. But in the past week, I've been demoing some new smart glasses from Samsung, Warby Parker, and Gentle Monster. Some are retro chic…
items.whyItMatters: Tech readers should track how privacy concerns shape wearable tech adoption.

items.title: Apple’s HomeView is my new favorite smart display — but not my daughter’s
items.summary: Apple’s HomeView smart display excels at home control, kitchen use, audio, and photo display, featuring Siri AI but with occasional slowness.
items.excerpt: Apple’s first smart display is finally here. And it’s good. | Photo: Hunter McRae for The Verge The HomeView nails everything I want from a smart display. It's superb at controlling my smart home; it's an excellent hands-free kitchen companion, a good speaker, and a gorgeous digital photo frame. It's also the first Apple smart speaker with Siri AI, which is an improvement, if still slow at times. But Apple has…
items.whyItMatters: Tech readers value Apple’s integration and design, but may question Siri’s performance and device suitability for families.

items.title: Sony’s latest Pulse wireless headset packs planar magnetic drivers at a good price
items.summary: Sony’s $99.99 PlayStation Pulse headset offers solid sound with planar magnetic drivers and essential features for gamers.
items.excerpt: It's tempting to seek out the do-everything wireless gaming headset with noise cancellation, phenomenal sound quality, multiplatform connectivity, swappable batteries - you name it. But if you just want the basics done well, Sony's new $99.99 PlayStation Pulse headset is worth considering. It has very good sound and just enough extras, even if you use more gadgets than just your PlayStation 5. Inside the Pulse's…
items.whyItMatters: It delivers good audio quality and key gaming features at a budget-friendly price.

items.title: Aura’s next color E Ink photo frame is smaller, cheaper, sharper, and more colorful
items.summary: Aura released a 10‑inch color E Ink photo frame with higher pixel density, more colors, a black frame, and a lower price of $349.

The new Aura Ink frame features a 10-inch E Ink panel that can display more colors at a higher pixel density. It's also differentiated from the original 13-inch model with a black frame and matching mat board that helps photos stand out. The Aura Ink 10 is now available in the US for $349, $150…
items.whyItMatters: Tech readers may value the improved display quality and cost savings for digital photo displays.

items.title: Peak Design’s Roller Lite Carry-On is bigger on the inside — and cheaper, too
items.summary: Peak Design released the Roller Lite Carry‑On, a cheaper, larger‑inside version of its earlier Roller Pro suitcase.
items.excerpt: When we sampled Peak Design's Roller Pro last year, we loved almost everything about the camera gear powerhouse's first attempt at a proper suitcase. Everything, that is, except for the price. Back then, during its crowdfunded launch, the Pro could be had for as little as $425. Today, you're looking at $599.95 for the same roller bag. Peak Design has taken that feedback to heart in creating the Roller Lite Carry-On…
items.whyItMatters: Tech‑savvy travelers will appreciate the improved capacity and lower price for premium luggage.

items.title: Hands-on with Ring’s new AI drone camera for your home
items.summary: Ring releases a flying indoor security camera, the Drone Cam, priced at $249.99 and shipping January 27, 2027.
items.excerpt: Ring’s new Drone Cam is a flying indoor security camera. Ring is finally shipping a flying indoor drone camera. For real this time. The Ring Drone Cam will arrive on January 27th, 2027, for $249.99, Ring founder Jamie Siminoff said at a launch event in New York City this week. If it does actually ship, it will arrive almost six years after the company announced its first flying camera, the Ring Always Home Cam…
items.whyItMatters: It adds autonomous aerial surveillance to home security, expanding Ring’s product line and offering new coverage angles.

items.title: Real Motors’ Project Ares is a cyberpunk fantasy made real
items.summary: Real Motors’ Project Ares showcases a fully electric motorcycle that blends retrofuturistic design with cutting‑edge technology, redefining motorcycle aesthetics.
items.excerpt: Electrification has done wonderful things for motorcycle design. By getting rid of the engine and the fuel tank that supports it, designers have the freedom to do whatever they want, and the results have been occasionally brilliant. I'm a big fan of the vaguely retrofuturistic stylings of the Maeving RM2 and the quirky minimalism of BMW's CE 02, but nothing yet has quite left me so awestruck as Project Ares. This…
items.whyItMatters: It demonstrates how electrification frees designers, offering new performance and style possibilities for tech‑savvy riders.
